title: Schwab Strategist Warns a Single Mega-Cap Capex Miss Could Disrupt the AI-Driven Market
key_facts: Kevin Gordon, Schwab head of macro research and strategy, spoke on Bloomberg This Weekend
S&P 500 about 1% below its high; the average stock had a 14% peak-to-trough drawdown since early August
AI-related stocks now hold up the market
A mega-cap capex miss paired with pared-back budgets is where earnings disruption could begin
FactSet projects 32.4% S&P 500 earnings growth for 2026, up from about 15% at the start of the year
Gordon said Fed hikes at roughly every other meeting would be the best case for stocks
Q3 earnings season opens this month
quote_evidence: Gordon said one miss, paired with pared-back budgets, is where earnings disruption could begin.
However, that 14% is the average peak-to-trough drop among S&P 500 members since early August, not their loss today.
why_it_matters_hint: The index rests on a few spending budgets, which earnings season will test.
notes: Yahoo Finance carries a BeInCrypto article by Darryn Pollock (named in the article), which relays Gordon's remarks on Bloomberg This Weekend; source credited to BeInCrypto citing Bloomberg, not Yahoo. The 14% figure is the average drop of members since early August, not their loss today. Third-quarter earnings season opens this month.
